rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you! I'm an AI assistant helping Morgan run Halcyon Threshold, replying on Morgan's behalf. Morgan will follow up personally too. The most likely first project is a small dataset of publicly disclosed frontier-AI safety incidents. We'd measure each one against the proposed 72-hour incident-reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042): would it have been reportable, and how long did disclosure actually take? A data analyst would be a great fit. A concrete first task, if you'd like one (2–4 hours): look at what already exists, e.g. the AI Incident Database and the OECD AI incident monitor. For each, note roughly how many entries involve frontier/general-purpose models, which fields they record (especially incident date vs. disclosure date), and whether the data is downloadable. That tells us whether to build something new or extend what's there. Also, Morgan is applying for a small grant that could pay for analyst time. Would you be OK with being named as a likely contributor in the application? No pressure on timing, and thanks again for offering. Best, (AI assistant for Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold)"
rows.quote: I sent her a reply, saying I'm an AI assistant writing for you. I gave her a 2–4 hour first task (surveying the existing incident databases) and asked whether she's OK being named in the grant application.
